items.name: Agent-Reach
items.description: MIT-licensed Python CLI (v1.5.0, 6.4k forks, 374 commits, last commit 2026-09-16) that installs, health-checks and routes to upstream tools so an agent can read and search the internet: web via Jina Reader, YouTube captions via yt-dlp, RSS, GitHub via gh, Exa semantic search via MCP, plus Twitter/X, Reddit, Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, and China-focused channels (Bilibili, Xiaohongshu, Xueqiu stocks, V2EX, Boss, Xiaoyuzhou podcasts). It is a glue layer, not a wrapper: after install the agent calls the upstream tools directly. Each platform has an ordered list of backends (first that really works wins) and `agent-reach doctor` reports which is live and how to fix the rest. Ships a SKILL.md with per-category reference files. Install is 'paste this URL to your agent'; default mode is read-only check, system changes need --system.
items.verdictNote: Mostly already covered. Do NOT install for web, YouTube, RSS, GitHub or search (you have Jina, Exa, Tavily, Firecrawl, Crawl4AI, SearXNG, Playwright, YouTube transcript MCP). Keep as an optional add-on for ONE gap: read-only Reddit and X research for finance-education and sports analytics, on a throwaway account, on an 8 GB GPU only. Steal its patterns now.
items.why: Ordered backends per capability, chosen by a REAL probe (does it actually return data), not just 'is the command installed'. Apply to the model router and to every data source in the swarm A `doctor` command that says which route is live and how to fix the rest. You should have one for the whole stack (local models, cloud models, database, automation) Safe-by-default installer: read-only check first, `--dry-run` preview, explicit flag for system changes, clean `uninstall` that removes stored credentials Credentials: stored in one file with 600 permissions, scrubbed from output, extracted from a browser one platform at a time (least privilege) Tests outnumber source: 606 pass, about 10.5k lines of tests for 7.3k lines of code; ruff and mypy both clean. A model for the Claude Code handoff standards URL guard written as 'public addresses only' using the standard library's is_global idea, covering odd IPv4 spellings. SEE : your own guard misses IPv6 and carrier-grade-NAT addresses Prompt-injection-aware install guide: explicit DO NOT list (no sudo, no system files, nothing inside the workspace) and fixed directories

warnings: ACCOUNT RISK: the X, Reddit, Instagram and Facebook routes use logged-in browser sessions or cookies, which breaks those platforms' terms. The author's own README says to use a throwaway account. Never connect your main brand accounts (Instagram, TikTok, etc.): a ban would hit your revenue brand
READ-ONLY ONLY: do not let any agent post, follow or message through these routes. That is the line between research and account-ban or spam territory
Third parties see the queries: Jina Reader receives every URL you read, Exa receives every search through its free MCP endpoint (free-tier limits and terms not verified)

'Paste this URL to your agent' installs from the moving `main` branch (pipx install of main.zip) with no pinned version. Treat install docs fetched by an agent as untrusted: pin a release tag and read the guide yourself first
Most channels target Chinese platforms (Bilibili, Xiaohongshu, Xueqiu, V2EX, Boss, Xiaoyuzhou) and are irrelevant to you unless you cover Chinese markets
Reddit has no zero-config route (anonymous access is blocked); it needs OpenCLI plus a desktop Chrome login, so it cannot run on the Windows server that hosts trading software
README includes sponsor ads and the author sells agent consulting; neither is a red flag, but 75k stars and a Trendshift badge are popularity, not an audit
One of 607 tests fails here only because this sandbox has GITHUB_TOKEN set; the test does not isolate the environment. Not a code bug

Platforms change anti-bot rules constantly; the project documents Bilibili blocking yt-dlp in June 2026 and a March 2026 wave of abandoned single-platform CLIs. Expect routes to break and rely on doctor
NOT RUN end to end: the sandbox cannot reach these platforms, so I verified code, tests and docs, not live scraping results

items.name: image-blaster
items.description: Claude Code skill pack (8 skills, 6 forked sub-agents, ~4,100 lines of Node scripts, no Python) that turns one image into: (1) GLB/OBJ meshes of each loose object via fal Hunyuan3D v3 (Meshy v6 optional), (2) a Gaussian-splat (.spz) of the empty static room plus a collider mesh via World Labs Marble 1.1, (3) ambient loop and per-object impact SFX via ElevenLabs on fal. Includes a React/three.js/Spark/Rapier viewer with a walkable character. Pipeline: analyse image -> list liftable objects (human confirms) -> remove them from the photo to make a clean plate -> generate world from the plate, generate each object from its own isolated reference image, generate SFX. The object step also works alone on any single image, without World Labs.
items.verdictNote: ADD as an optional pay-per-use specialist tool. Use the object-to-mesh step and the SFX step now (cheap, no World Labs dependency); HOLD the World Labs step until the AMD deal and API commercial terms are clear. Run a pilot with a hard fal spend cap only after the indie web-game 2D/3D question is answered. Copy its patterns into your own skills regardless.
items.why: FILLS A GAP, replaces nothing: you had no hosted image-to-mesh tool. Free local alternative is Trellis2 via ComfyUI, but it shares the 8 GB card with Flux and VoiceStudio NOT RUN: no API keys and the sandbox cannot reach the providers, so mesh and world quality are the README's claims, not the result. Pilot before relying on it WORLD LABS RISK: AMD announced an $8.2B all-stock acquisition on 2026-09-28 (AMD newsroom, Bloomberg, CNBC; close expected end of 2026). Neither side has committed to Marble API pricing or continuity, and the Terms already allow suspension and assignment. Do not build a revenue path on the World API yet WORLD LABS COMMERCIAL RIGHTS UNVERIFIED: docs name only the Pro app plan as including commercial rights to generated worlds; nothing found for API-generated outputs. Read the API terms before any paid release README overstates 'fully meshed environment': code downloads only the collider mesh (a collision proxy) plus splats; the HQ mesh export is a separate $2.80 and the code does not call it Default object meshes are 50,000 faces with PBR: too heavy for phones and browser games; use LowPoly generate type and Blender cleanup. AI meshes are unrigged by default (Meshy option adds rigging) Price (fal and World Labs docs, Oct 2026, subject to change): world 1,500 credits = $1.20 (+80 credits pano = $0.064); Hunyuan3D v3 $0.375 base + $0.15 PBR + $0.15 custom face count = about $0.675 per object; Nano Banana 2 edit $0.08 (1K); SFX $0.002/s. A scene with 8 objects is roughly $7.50 first pass, before retries and Claude tokens Hunyuan via fal is listed as commercial use under fal terms; the open-weights Hunyuan licence excludes EU/UK/South Korea for self-hosting - fal's hosted route is the one priced here, but read fal terms before shipping Code quality: clean, modular, resumable (provider request id saved before polling), base64 stripped from logs, key in gitignored.env, typecheck passes (exit 0), 11 of 13 tests pass. BUT: zero timeouts or retries anywhere (two infinite polling loops), provider error bodies discarded (only the HTTP status is kept), ~4,100 lines of pipeline scripts with no tests, and the 2 failing tests only check that API keys are set Single maintainer, last commit 2026-05-14 (five months ago), 72 commits; 4.8k stars and 494 forks show interest, not production hardening Dependency licences checked: Spark, three, fiber, drei, leva, Radix, zustand MIT; postprocessing Zlib; the Rapier wrapper declares no licence field in its package.json (not checked further)
items.license: MIT (repo). Output rights come from the paid APIs, not the repo: see caveats

items.name: Papermorph
items.description: Claude Code skill (npx skills add DozenTwelve/Papermorph; 36 commits, 0 forks, no releases, one author) that turns a PDF into a static web book of chapters. Each chapter is a 1600x900 SVG 'stage' driven by a deterministic timeline: the narration is split into beats (mp3 + timed actions), [[mark]] tags in the script become word-start times from the TTS word boundaries, and every on-screen element (move, draw, pop, highlight, stream) is tweened from those times. Quiz cards (choice, blanks, grid, tap, sorter) sit between beats. No build step; progress saved in the browser. A review loop (contact-sheet screenshots, blank-opening checker, keyboard test, one fresh sub-agent per chapter with file-based state) is part of the skill. Visual style is a dark chalkboard.
items.verdictNote: ADD as a specialist tool for content studio plus a pattern source. Worth it for short, accurate, diagram-style explainers where a prompt-to-video model cannot be trusted with numbers or text (finance, math, rules of a game). Not a replacement for Seedance/Kling-style footage. Do not use as-is: it needs (1) the exporter step to become video, (2) a licensed or local voice instead of Edge TTS, (3) a small finance shape library. Pilot one finance-education explainer first, then decide.
items.why: RUN: the sample site loads and plays in this sandbox with no page errors; 42 frames viewed across a chapter. Narration quality and chapter-generation cost were NOT measured (no Opus tokens spent on generating a new chapter) IT IS A WEB BOOK, NOT A VIDEO TOOL. It has no export to MP4. I wrote a prototype exporter (tools/papermorph_render_beats.py): it opens a beat, calls the engine's own evalTo(t) for each frame, screenshots only the stage, and pipes frames plus the beat's mp3 into ffmpeg. Result: 1920x1080 30 fps MP4 with narration, deterministic and frame-exact. Speed here (CPU only): about 11 frames per second, roughly 2.6x real time, so a 5-minute lesson renders in about 13 minutes. Prototype: no resume, no caption burn-in, beats must be stitched with ffmpeg, tested on one beat of one chapter VOICE LICENCE RISK: narration uses Edge TTS, an unofficial route to Microsoft's Read Aloud service. A Microsoft Q&A moderator statement (Oct 2024) says commercial use without an Azure subscription may violate the terms. Swap before any monetised video: the local VoiceStudio/Supertonic tiers, Azure AI Speech, or ElevenLabs. The swap needs word timings for [[mark]] sync; VoiceStudio lists transcription but word-level timestamps are untested Young and tiny: 1 star, created recently, one maintainer; README says it currently supports Opus 5.5 only. Treat as a code-and-ideas source, pin a commit, expect breakage Quality is bounded by the model's storyboards: layouts are generated per chapter, so every chapter needs the review loop. Built for textbook math; finance visuals would need a helper library you do not have yet Opus-heavy by design (long skill, one sub-agent per chapter): token cost per minute of video is unknown. Measure on one pilot before planning volume MIT licence covers the code; any book/PDF you feed it keeps its own copyright, so only use your own scripts or public-domain/licensed text UPDATE Oct 13: HyperFrames (Apache-2.0, 59k stars) is a maintained renderer for HTML timelines and I ran it, so you should not maintain your own exporter for new explainers. Papermorph stays the pattern source for narration-mark timelines and interactive web lessons; its own engine (not GSAP) would need a small adapter to render through HyperFrames

Four skills: motion-design (numeric easing and stagger rules), review-loop (render a draft, tile one frame per timeline beat into labelled contact sheets, check collisions, clipping, safe area, readability, fix, repeat), sound-design (Python cue sheets that synthesise pops and whooshes with the standard library and master to -14 LUFS, true peak under -2 dBFS; example has 128 sounds), web-sims. items.name: claude-motion-design
items.description: Skill by howseen-ai (17 commits, last Oct 2). One seek(t) function draws every frame (no CSS transitions or timers); Playwright captures frames, several sub-frames per frame are blended with ffmpeg tmix for motion blur; encoded BT.709 TV-range; single-frame 'pop' detection; sound is music plus effects only: drop found by band energy, effects placed at measured peaks, two-pass loudness to -14 LUFS. No voice-over. Same architecture as the exporter I prototyped for Papermorph.
items.verdictNote: REFERENCE: HyperFrames already does the capture; steal the motion-blur and encode settings.
items.why: 0 stars; determinism and 'every effect lands on its peak' are claims, not tests fetch_assets.py downloads from Mixkit, Pexels, Unsplash, svgl and simple-icons: licences are per asset, check before commercial use mcp21_client.py calls 21st.dev's API Serves the project over python http.server: bind to localhost

items.name: knowledge-work-plugins
items.description: Anthropic's official plugins for knowledge work: sales, marketing, finance, legal, data, design, product management, HR, customer support, operations, bio-research and more. Each plugin bundles skills, slash commands, sub-agents and MCP connectors as plain markdown and JSON. Built for Claude's agentic workspace and Claude Code. 252 SKILL.md files; last commit 2026-10-21.
items.verdictNote: have: install per role from the plugin catalog; customize rather than fork
items.why: Official and actively maintained. The plugin format is also the best template for packaging your own workflows: copy the folder layout when you build a plugin. Connectors only work for apps you actually connect.

items.name: Cloudflare security-audit skill
items.description: Single skill that turns a coding agent into a security auditor for one repo. Six phases: reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting by isolated agents, independent validation that tries to disprove every finding, schema-checked findings.json, re-verification, and a report. Covers web/auth, AI and prompt injection, supply chain, cloud, client-side and memory safety. Seed of Cloudflare's vulnerability harness. Last commit 2026-09-14.
items.verdictNote: adopt: run on your own repos before shipping anything public or paid
items.why: Defensive and well designed: a separate verifier must fail to disprove each finding, which cuts false alarms. Many sub-agents means a large token bill per run, so audit one repo at a time and re-run only on changes.

items.name: Claude-Red
items.description: Library of about 79 offensive-security SKILL.md files: web app testing, Active Directory, cloud, wireless, exploit development. Its SECURITY.md limits use to authorized red-team, pentest and bug-bounty work with written permission. Has an install.sh. Last commit 2026-10-12.
items.verdictNote: reference: only for authorized testing of systems you own or have written permission to test
items.why: Useful to understand how attackers approach your own stack, but it is attack methodology, not a defensive tool. For checking your own code, use the Cloudflare security-audit skill instead. Read install.sh before running it.

items.name: Android skills (official)
items.description: Google's official SKILL.md set for Android development, based on developer.android.com: build system, Jetpack Compose, CameraX, navigation, performance, security, testing, on-device AI, Wear OS, TV, cars and XR. 33 skills; last commit 2026-10-23.
items.verdictNote: reference: install only when you start an Android or Wear OS app
items.why: Authoritative and current, so it beats generic Android advice from a model. Not useful until there is an Android project; ESP32 or web projects don't need it.

items.name: scientific-agent-skills (K-Dense)
items.description: 177 skills for scientific research: bioinformatics, chemistry, medicine, data analysis, literature search and scientific writing; works with several agent hosts. Includes skill security-scan scripts. The vendor sells commercial support and a hosted platform. Last commit 2026-10-19.
items.verdictNote: reference: pick single skills (data analysis, scientific writing); don't install all 177
items.why: Large and well organized, but mostly lab-science domains. Installing everything bloats the skill list; copy only the few that match your work. Its scan_skills.py is a good pattern for vetting third-party skills.

items.name: text-to-cad
items.description: Plugin and 13 skills that let coding agents create and edit real CAD parts from text or images on Open CASCADE (build123d). Exports STEP, STL, 3MF and GLB; also dimensioned engineering drawings (PDF), DXF, G-code, URDF/SRDF/SDF robot files, design-for-manufacturing and 3D-printing checks, and hand-offs to Bambu Lab printers and SendCutSend. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini. Needs uv, Python 3.11+, Node 20+. About 1,460 commits; last 2026-10-20.
items.verdictNote: trial: start with one printable bracket or enclosure and check the STEP in a CAD viewer
items.why: Produces real, editable engineering geometry (STEP), not a mesh, which is what printing, CNC and robot simulation actually need. On Windows 11, Smart App Control blocks its native CAD module: turn it off or run under WSL. Always measure critical dimensions before ordering parts.

items.name: marketingskills (Corey Haines)
items.description: 52 marketing skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other Agent Skills hosts: copywriting, CRO, SEO and AI-search SEO, programmatic SEO, ads and ad creative, email and cold email, launch, pricing, lead magnets, referrals, churn, analytics, social, video and more. A shared product-marketing skill holds your positioning and every other skill reads it first. Includes validation scripts and tool-integration notes. Last commit 2026-10-19.
items.verdictNote: adopt: install, fill in product-marketing once per brand, then use the few skills you need
items.why: The best-maintained open marketing skill set: practical frameworks, one shared positioning file, and very active. Covers more than the official marketing plugin for growth tactics. Install selectively; 52 skills is a lot to keep loaded.

items.name: digital-marketing-agents 1.0
items.description: /market command suite of 19 skills plus agents for SEO, conversion, competitor analysis, copy, email, social, launch and proposals, with a GTM context file and install/uninstall scripts. Single commit, last updated 2026-04-02.
items.verdictNote: reference: borrow the GTM-context file idea; use coreyhaines31/marketingskills instead
items.why: Sensible layout but one commit, 4 stars and no updates since April. The installer can be run via curl | bash, so read it first. The Corey Haines set does the same job and is maintained.

items.name: Marketing-Skills (Cesarjoquin)
items.description: Re-packaged copy of coreyhaines31/marketingskills (45 skills) with an added TypeScript CLI, Redis caching, tests and CI. Not marked as a GitHub fork. Last commit 2026-09-14.
items.verdictNote: skip: use the original coreyhaines31/marketingskills
items.why: Behind the original (45 vs 52 skills, a month older) and the extra CLI only matters for engineers. Two copies of the same skills just confuse the agent.

items.name: agents-agencia-marketing (ASV Digital)
items.description: 57 Claude Code sub-agents for running a Brazilian marketing agency (proposals, pricing, onboarding, SLAs, sprints, QBRs, profitability), in Portuguese, shipped as zip files. One commit (2026-05-05).
items.verdictNote: skip: not open-licensed and Portuguese-only
items.why: The README restricts use to the vendor's clients and forbids redistribution, so you can't legally build on it. The agency-operations topics are a useful checklist only.

items.name: claude-skills (Alireza Rezvani)
items.description: Very large skill library (about 465 SKILL.md files, roughly 5,800 files) across 20 domains: engineering, product, project management, marketing, finance, compliance and regulatory/quality, C-level advisory and agents, business operations and growth, research. Skills bundle instructions, Python helper scripts and templates; works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and others. Very active (commit 2026-10-23). The README's skill and star counts contradict each other.
items.verdictNote: assess: cherry-pick a few (product, project management, C-level advisor); never install the whole library
items.why: Broad coverage of business roles a PM or consultant uses, under MIT. Quality varies across hundreds of skills and many run Python scripts, so read each one before installing. Loading too many skills makes agents pick the wrong one.

items.name: Growth Marketing OS
items.description: Free English and Arabic library of AI marketing assets by a working growth marketer: 25 prompts, 8 original plus 11 community Claude skills, 2 agents and 3 Custom GPT setups, 7 benchmark sheets with cited sources, swipe files (hooks, subject lines, CTAs, WhatsApp scripts), playbooks, worked examples, an SEO/GEO setup guide and one MCP recipe. Focus on e-commerce, SaaS and paid ads in the Middle East (including cash-on-delivery stores). 97 commits; last 2026-10-10.
items.verdictNote: reference: use the cited benchmarks and swipe files; get skills from coreyhaines31/marketingskills
items.why: Honest and small: it lists its own gaps (no case studies yet, n8n workflow not exported). The sourced 'is this number good?' benchmarks are the most useful part. Prompts and skills overlap with bigger sets, and the regional focus (Egypt, GCC) matters only if you sell there.

items.name: threejs-game-skills (Majid Manzarpour)
items.description: 9 skills for building browser games in three.js: a game-director entry point, gameplay systems (controls, camera, physics, game feel), AAA graphics/VFX, game UI designer (HUDs, menus, pause/win screens, touch controls), debug/profiler, QA and release, plus optional generators for 3D (Tripo), images (Gemini) and audio (ElevenLabs). The UI skill has about 3.3k installs on skills.sh. 11 commits.
items.verdictNote: trial: best single pack for three.js web games; core skills work without paid keys
items.why: One author, one coherent pipeline, unlike mixing skills from different sources. The asset generators need paid API keys (Tripo, Gemini, ElevenLabs) but fall back to procedural assets without them. Only 11 commits, so pin a version.

items.name: game-feel (jarrodmedrano)
items.description: Consulting-style skill based on Steve Swink's book Game Feel: helps design responsive controls, hit-stop, camera shake and feedback. About 51 installs; passed the Gen Agent Trust Hub, Socket and Snyk checks on skills.sh.
items.verdictNote: reference: read it for the framework; the gamedev packs already cover game feel
items.why: Grounded in a respected book, but tiny usage. awesome-gamedev-agent-skills and threejs-game-skills both include game-feel guidance already.

items.name: game-design-theory (akillness)
items.description: Skill from akillness/jeo-skills that turns a design question into a testable 'theory packet' using MDA, player motivation, decision structure, feedback/resource loops and mastery, then designs a small prototype to test it.
items.verdictNote: reference: good method for testing a mechanic before building it
items.why: Useful discipline (test why a loop is fun before building it), but a small repo (47 stars). Several unrelated skills share the name 'game-design-theory'; install from the named source only.

items.name: higgsfield-websites (Higgsfield AI)
items.description: Official Higgsfield skill that generates site code and assets from a brief, with Blender-based 3D conversion and rigging, video processing and brand assets, using Higgsfield's generation APIs. Rated SAFE by Gen Agent Trust Hub (2026-09-26), with notes: installs via curl piped to sh, downloads a portable Blender, and passes briefs into prompts unsanitised.
items.verdictNote: assess: only worth it if you already pay for Higgsfield
items.why: It is a front end for Higgsfield's paid generation service, not a free asset pipeline. Free asset sources plus your own deploy route do the same job without lock-in.

items.name: MotionSites Web Builder (Claude skill)
items.description: Free Claude skill/plugin from MotionSites (Viktor Oddy): 40 most-liked website prompts, a media shelf of 50+ AI hero videos, 30 3D cut-outs and 29 images on CloudFront, 58 technique recipes (liquid glass, blur headlines, scroll-scrubbed video, Three.js), taste rules with numbers, a spec template, and a Playwright screenshot-and-fix loop (shoot.py). Paid MotionSites plans: $49 pack, $129/3 months, $279/year, $399 lifetime, with an MCP for the premium library.
items.verdictNote: trial: strong landing-page workflow; expect an upsell block in every answer
items.why: The spec-first and screenshot-and-fix loop raise AI-built pages well above default output, and the technique recipes are reusable. The skill instructs Claude to append a MotionSites upgrade ad to every delivery (you can tell it to stop), and the hosted videos are MotionSites' own, so swap in your own media for client work.
items.license: MIT (instructions/code); example prompts and media (c) MotionSites

items.name: anatomy (isometric machine figures)
items.description: Claude Code / agent skill that draws detailed isometric figures of real machines and systems as SVG, as a standalone HTML page, a lone SVG or React components; optional WebGL shader effects (fire, water) and a beta 3D mode. Install with `npx skills add wheresryan22/anatomy -g`. Node 20.10+, no API keys, no npm install. Companion repo of 52 ready figures.
items.verdictNote: trial: explainer figures for articles, landing pages and Shorts thumbnails
items.why: Fills a gap nothing else in the library covers: clean technical illustrations (engines, devices, systems) without a designer. Free and keyless. Check each figure for technical accuracy before publishing.
